title: Coordinate averaging preserves expectation
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. Define $E_i g(x)=\frac{g(x_{i\leftarrow 0})+g(x_{i\leftarrow 1})}{2}$, where $x_{i\leftarrow b}$ is obtained by setting coordinate $i$ to $b$. Then $\mathbb E_x[E_i g(x)]=\mathbb E_x[g(x)]$ under the uniform measure.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Let $g$ be a real cube function and $i\in[n]$, and define $E_i g(x)=\tfrac12(g(x_{i\leftarrow0})+g(x_{i\leftarrow1}))$, where the indicated update replaces bit $i$. Then $\mathbb E[E_i g]=\mathbb E g$.
